Samantha — great to hear, and thanks for the clear list. Recap + proposed next steps below so your team can act quickly.

Recap from our call
- Primary corpus: research articles + regulatory PDFs (~300 doc pilot)
- Critical success criteria: answer precision on regulatory Qs, low hallucination on provenance-sensitive outputs, <= 200ms median token latency for interactive UI

Recommendations (short list)
1) Model family: start with a smaller instruction-tuned open model for iteration speed and cost (e.g., redwood-compat-7B-qa) for development; for benchmark and production target the 13B instruction-tuned variant (redwood-13B-instruct-v2) to evaluate quality delta. We can provide exact docker images/weights for both.
2) Retrieval defaults to try: chunk size 400–600 tokens with 50-token overlap; embed at paragraph granularity where possible. Start with ANN top_k=100 (recall sweep) and serve top_n=10 to the reranker.
3) Reranker choice: for Ambrosia's accuracy bar we recommend a cross-encoder reranker for the pilot (higher precision at cost of compute). If latency/cost becomes restrictive, switch to a hybrid: bi-encoder candidate pruning + small cross-encoder re-rank of top-10. See attached "reranker-pros-cons.pdf" for tradeoffs.
4) Grounding metrics & eval suite: we'll use a combination of retrieval recall@k, passage-level grounding rate (fraction of answers with an explicit citation), and a hallucination audit (annotated sample). Not relying solely on LM perplexity — see "eval-prompt-set-v1.txt" attached with baseline prompts and edge-case prompts for regulatory QA.

Action items (we can support these):
- Redwood: share a ready-to-run eval kit (Drive link below) + initial config CSV for retrieval settings. (I attached "retrieval-configs.csv" with starting values.)
- Ambrosia: populate the sandbox bucket with a labeled set of 100 QA pairs for first-pass regression checks.
- Schedule: proposed POC kickoff week of 2027-07-05; let us know constraints.

I'll let Karthik add the more detailed retrieval/reranker tuning steps below. Happy to run the kickoff with Ben (Solutions) and Karthik (ML).

Thanks,
Irene

Great questions — adding some concrete numbers and test plan details.

Technical tuning notes (recommend starting sweep):
- Tokenization & chunking: 400–600 token chunks work well for dense retrieval on scientific PDFs; set overlap = 20–60 tokens correlated with average paragraph length. For highly structured regulatory docs (sections + appendices) consider a section-aware chunker (split on headings) to preserve provenance.
- Vector index & recall: use HNSW with ef_search=128 for recall sweeps, index ef_construction=200. Start with top_k retrieval candidates = 100; measure recall@100 vs recall@10 to understand drop-off.
- Reranker: run an ablation between
  * bi-encoder (fast) using sentence-transformers (cheap) to rerank top_100 -> top_20, then cross-encoder to finalize top_5, and
  * pure cross-encoder (roberta-cross-v3) on top_100 -> top_10 (more expensive but higher precision).
  Expect ~6–12% absolute improvement in exact-citation precision from adding a cross-encoder on top of a bi-encoder baseline in our benchmarks.
- Latency economics: cross-encoder cost scales linearly with candidates; keep cross-encoder input to <=10 to control compute. Hybrid approach often gives best cost/quality tradeoff.

Evaluation checklist (what we'll run in POC)
- Retrieval recall sweep (k={10,50,100}) on 300-doc sandbox using held-out questions.
- Reranker ablation: bi-encoder only vs hybrid vs cross-encoder-only, measure citation precision, MRR, and grounding_rate.
- Regression watch: store evaluation artifacts (prompts, seed hashes, model_version) and run nightly batch checks; trigger a pager if grounding_rate drops >5% relative to baseline.

Artifacts I'm attaching / links:
- Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB2cRedwood/ambrosia-rag-eval (contains eval-prompt-set, runner scripts)
- Short benchmark summary: https://bench.redwood.ai/rag/ambrosia-summary

If you want, Ben can coordinate getting a sandbox token and a one-off config applied to your test index so you can run the first recall sweep by next week.

-Karthik
